stories.title: Phase 13: AWS-verified SCP/RCP semantics grounding doc
requirements: Research + write docs/scp-rcp-semantics.md (AWS-verified, cite sources). SCP (Service Control Policy): a permission CEILING on member accounts - it constrains the MAXIMUM available permissions and NEVER grants; an action is effective only if allowed by an identity policy AND permitted (not denied, and within any SCP Allow) by every applicable SCP. Cover: Deny guardrails; SCP Allow-list ceilings; NotAction complements in SCPs (Deny NotAction = deny everything EXCEPT the listed, do NOT read the list as allowed); aws:RequestedRegion region guardrails with global-service exceptions; StringNotEqualsIfExists behavior in Deny. RCP (Resource Control Policy): org-level guardrails on RESOURCES, deny-only, set a ceiling on who may access org resources; confused-deputy at org scope (aws:SourceOrgID, aws:PrincipalIsAWSService, aws:SourceAccount presence via Null); RCPs never grant.

State the load-bearing invariant reused from the permissions-boundary ceiling family: an SCP/RCP Allow is a CEILING, not a grant - the analyzer must NEVER manufacture a positive capability finding/edge from an SCP/RCP. No shipped-code change in this story.

stories.title: Phase 14: KMS key-policy per-service finding rules
requirements: Add KMS per-service rules (dispatch on kms-key) per docs/resource-per-service-semantics.md section 3: (a) a Principal '*' KMS key policy is NOT anonymous - KMS has no unauthenticated path; report it as 'usable by every AWS identity in every account (cross-account still double-authorized)' and DROP all 'anonymous / unauthenticated / anyone on the internet' wording that the generic PUBLIC-ACCESS finding uses; Resource:'*' = the attached key only. (b) kms:CallerAccount is a principal-account scoping key (narrows a '*' to authenticated identities in the named account, like aws:PrincipalAccount); kms:ViaService is a SERVICE-CHANNEL selector that narrows the request vector, NOT the principal - a '*' narrowed only by kms:ViaService is still account-open and must not read as scoped-to-account/authenticated-only.

(c) Rank dangerous KMS actions: kms:Decrypt/GenerateDataKey*/ReEncrypt* to '*' or cross-account = data-plane exposure; kms:PutKeyPolicy = key-policy takeover; kms:CreateGrant = an onward-DELEGATION primitive (the grantee can create grants letting other principals in any account/org use the key and need not hold the permission itself) - name it as delegation, never as proven decrypt or effective access; kms:GrantIsForAWSResource narrows CreateGrant.
